 Weekend Briefing 
 November 6, 2026 
 IMAGES IN CLINICAL MEDICINE 
 A 56-year-old woman was referred to the hepatobiliary surgery clinic with abnormal liver imaging. She reported fatigue and chronic epistaxis. Telangiectasias were seen on physical examination. Read the article.

 PERSPECTIVE
 Mass Surveillance with Artificial Intelligence — A New Determinant of Health? 
 N. Peoples, K. Hoops, and E.W. Fleegler
 AI is changing the fundamental nature of surveillance in ways that strain existing privacy law and put public health at risk. Medicine has a responsibility to confront these developments. Read the article. 
 PERSPECTIVE
 Equity in Maternal–Fetal Medicine — Technological Advances and a Potential Path Forward 
 D. Mallampati, C. Binion, and N.L. Vora
 Without safeguards, rapid technological development in maternal–fetal medicine could reinforce existing racial, socioeconomic, and geographic inequities in prenatal care. Read the article. 
 PERSPECTIVE
 Early Days, Late Nights

 TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features 
 P. Généreux and Others
 In patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, the percentage who died or had a heart-failure event within 2 years was lower with transcatheter aortic-valve replacement than with surveillance (16.7% vs. 23.9%). Read the article.

 Private Health Insurance and Profit — Lessons for the United States 
 I. Papanicolas and J.F. Figueroa
